statement: How many different 1 by 3 strips of three squares, going across or down, can be found on a 4 by 4 grid?

choices.misconception: I counted how many strips fit on the grid at the same time without overlapping.
I only counted the strips that go across.
I thought a strip can start in any of the first 3 squares of a row or column.
I counted each strip twice, once from each end.

hints: How many places can a strip slide to in one row?
Strips may overlap, so slide a strip along one row and count its positions. Every row and every column works the same way, so multiply, and remember both directions.
In a row of 4 squares, a strip of 3 can start in square 1 or square 2.

solutions.reliable: In one row of 4 squares, a 1 by 3 strip fits in 4 - 3 + 1 = 2 positions. There are 4 rows, giving 8 strips across, and by the same reasoning 8 strips down. Total 16. The transferable idea: count positions by sliding, not by cutting the grid up.

whyOnTest: Sliding-window counting: overlapping positions count, so cutting the grid into pieces undercounts.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
